newsitem.title: USA: DuPont sues Millennium Chemicals over patent.
newsitem.headline: DuPont sues Millennium Chemicals over patent.

text.p: Chemical giant DuPont Co. sued Millennium Chemicals Inc. in federal court, accusing its rival of infringing a DuPont patent involving titanium dioxide pigment.
In papers filed late Thursday in U.S. District Court in Delaware, DuPont said its 1994 patent is being infringed by a Millenium product sold as Tiona RCL-188.

Wilmington, Del.-based DuPont is the largest producer of titanium dioxide pigment in the United States and worldwide. Millennium is the second largest producer of the product, also known as white pigment, in the United States.
Millennium, based in Iselin, N.J., was spun off from Hanson Plc in October. Millennium Inorganic Chemicals Inc., a subsidiary formerly known as SCM Chemicals, is also named as a defendant.

DuPont seeks an accounting of Millennium's profits from the alleged infringement, unspecified damages tripled for alleged wilful infringement, and an injunction barring further production of the product.
A Millennium spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
DuPont stock rose $4.125 to $107.375 Friday and Millenium climbed 75 cents to $18.375, both in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
